sections.body: This field covers ten areas where artificial intelligence is changing research and teaching. AI now reads and summarizes large collections of papers for literature review, maps citations to show how ideas connect, and runs statistical tests or reproduces analyses. It also helps code interview transcripts, draft grant sections, check writing, design course materials, organize research data, run lab simulations, and flag integrity problems. The work is practical, not theoretical, and the site links to original papers rather than a search tool.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are now routine, like searching and summarizing papers, but others remain unreliable. Literature review tools can miss relevant work, citation mapping can overstate connections, and quantitative analysis still needs human checking for reproducibility. Qualitative coding and grant writing help with drafts but do not replace judgment. Laboratory automation and simulation are useful for planning but cannot guarantee real-world results. The honest limit is that AI can speed up parts of research, not do the thinking or take responsibility for it. The site's library holds 135 research papers and 10767 extracted claims, which shows a large but uneven evidence base.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from finding and understanding prior work to doing new work and then checking it. Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis and Citation Mapping and Discovery help a reader see what has been done and how it connects. Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods cover the two main ways of analyzing data. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review address the writing and review parts of research. Course Design and Teaching and Research Data and Repositories cover teaching and data management. Laboratory Automation and Simulation and Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity close with the physical and rule-based sides of research, and a reader would go to each page for the specific task named in its title.
